etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From ちっと (chitto), itself a geminated emphatic form of ちと (chito), originally composed of ち (chi, “small”, not used in isolation; cognate with the chi in 小さい chīsai) + と (to, adverbial particle).
First attested in 1477.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Reduplication of onomatopoeic root どき (doki), unattested in isolation. Reduplicated form どきどき (dokidoki) first attested in 1700.
Similar, but apparently unrelated, to Sino-Japanese term 動悸 (dōki, “heartbeat; palpitation”). That term is not attested until 1721.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The prefix 不(ふ) (fu-) + 可(か) (ka).

etymologies.text: 世 (yo) + の (no) + 中 (naka)

etymologies.text: Learned borrowing from Chinese 代表 (dàibiǎo).

etymologies.text: 停留(ていりゅう) (teiryū) + 所(しょ) (-sho, rendaku form 所(じょ) (jo))

etymologies.text: 先 is a daiyōji replacing 尖.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From the 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “continuative or stem form”) of the nari-adjective 大(おお)い (ōi).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 太陽 (MC thajH yang, “sun”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Phrase consisting of 女 (onna, “female person, woman”) + の (no, appositive particle) + 人 (hito, “person”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From tei (定, fixed) + ka (価, monetary value).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: This spelling is probably ateji (当(あ)て字(じ)). See the main entry for further details.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 弱(よわ) (yowa, root of 弱(よわ)い (yowai, “weak”)) + まる (-maru, “to become (an adjective); -en”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From 形(けい)容(よう) (keiyō, “description; form”) + 詞(し) (-shi, “word; part of speech”).
First cited to 1870.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
手 (shu, “hand”) + 術 (-jutsu, “technique”).
Presumably a Meiji period calque of Ancient Greek χειρουργία (kheirourgía).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Learned borrowing from Middle Chinese 文明 (MC mjun mjaeng).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Back-formation of 月曜日(げつようび) (getsuyōbi), 火曜日(かようび) (kayōbi), etc.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 極 (MC gik).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Reduplication of 次(つぎ) (tsugi, “next; following”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Orthographic borrowing from Chinese 歌謠／歌谣 (gēyáo).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese mazu, first attested in the Nihon Shoki of 720.
Reconstructed as deriving from Proto-Japonic *mansu. Cognate with Okinawan 混じゆん (majiyun).

etymologies.text: 生(い)き (iki, stem of 生きる (ikiru, “to live”)) + 物(もの) (-mono, “thing”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Cognate with 成る (naru, “become”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 目(め) (me, “eye”) + 上(うえ) (ue, “above”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Shift from older 真白 (mashiro), with gemination as an excrescence to express emphasis. First cited to around 1500.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 編(あ)み (ami, 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 編(あ)む (amu, “to knit”)) + 物(もの) (-mono, “thing”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 茶色(ちゃいろ) (chairo) + い (-i).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
*/kuwu/ → /kuweru/ → /kʷeru/ → /keru/
From Old Japanese verb 蹴う (kuu), from Proto-Japonic *kuw-a-.
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.
The conjugation shifted from 下二段活用 (shimo nidan katsuyō, “bigrade conjugation”) (/kuwe-/, /kuu/) to 下一段活用 (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “monograde conjugation”) (/kʷe-/, /kʷeru/) in Early Middle Japanese. This verb was the only shimo ichidan verb in Early Middle Japanese.
Pronunciation of /kʷe/ changed to /ke/ before around 1300.
The conjugation irregularly shifted from 下一段活用 (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “monograde conjugation”) (/ke-/, /keru/) to 四段活用 (yodan katsuyō, “quadrigrade conjugation”) (/ker-/, /keru/) after the early Edo period. Remnants of the monograde conjugation can still be seen in various compounds, such as 足蹴(あしげ) (ashige) or 蹴落(けお)とす (keotosu), which include the obsolete ren'yōkei 蹴(け) (ke) (modern 蹴(け)り (keri)).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese, ultimately from Proto-Japonic *kankay. Cognate with 影(かげ) (kage, “shadow”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 陰 (ʔˠiɪm).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/hoto₂/: *[potə] → [ɸoto] → [hoto].
As indicated in the Wamyōshō citation, /to₂/ may be related to 処(と) (/to₁/, “place, location”), but the phonological difference can not be explained. Perhaps related to Korean 보지 (boji, “vagina”).
